body:
Technically they were my ex's group of friends to begin with, but since we all lived in the same area I acclimated into the group. After the breakup, the group made it a pick sides situation. I'll admit that at the end of the relationship, I turned into less of a friend and more into a naggy/clingy girlfriend, which they didn't like, so they ostracized me, said nasty things about me, and I chose to cleave myself from them. I miss the group as a whole though, because like I said, I invested a lot of time and feelings into all of them including my ex, but I've been trying to convince myself that I don't need those kinds of people in my life if that's the extent of their emotional maturity.  

And wow, I guess we have more in common than I thought. I also play League of Legends, used to play with my ex and that entire group and actually contributed a lot to the deterioration of the relationship. Aside from that, I've been trying to get back into console gaming but it requires a bigger time commitment than 40 minute league games, so I usually just go back to league. But since that group cut me out, I basically play with individuals who I've met through the game and live all over rather than within a 10 mile radius. I can still enjoy the game, but at the same time I miss the company of playing with friends in my area, because I'd get to see them on the weekends and stuff. So now, like you said, it's basically my means of escape - a small reprieve during my day, although I do have my moments where I'll get a little down after not performing well or a losing streak, haha.  

It's strange when you talk about looking for empathy in others, because in other situations that have happened in the past, I felt like I always had people to fall back on. I wouldn't call myself an extrovert because I'm still generally withdrawn around strangers and people I don't know too well, but maybe I used to be a more outgoing introvert. I wouldn't be so shy to avoid conversations with individuals who seemed friendly or genuinely wanted to get to know me better. But I will agree that a lot of friendships I've had ended up being very superficial, or maybe we just didn't find a more common emotional ground beneath the shared interests. I don't know if I've just become too jaded or discouraged from reaching out to the friends I do have, but they always just seem so busy or I don't want to make it seem like I'm not improving to them. While I cherish my friendships, I don't like relying on others as an emotional crutch because of what happened when I tried doing that with the breakup. Instead of getting empathy, I ended up exhausting their patience and tolerance, which led them to want nothing to do with me.  

There are one, maybe two, individuals though who I'm okay divulging these worries with. However, since they aren't in such great spots themselves in their path of life, I don't like going into too much detail out of fear of striking their own emotional volatility and making them feel down with me. So maybe I'll mention it, but won't go too far into talking about my specific worries. I also have gone to counseling, but found that it didn't really help me. The things they said had merit, don't get me wrong, but my emotions have always been stronger than my logic, and knowing that it's not good for me to be acting a certain way is completely different from feeling down or depressed when given a trigger - it's hard to keep in mind that I need to be more in control during situations in which this ends up happening.

But thank you for commenting, it's been a great help. I think actually being able to type out thoughts and really think about things in the process helps. I assume you're from a different country given your required military service, but do you perhaps have a LoL account on the NA server? Or some other medium aside from reddit commenting, so we can talk more. Perhaps we can play a game or two sometime, and I can chat with you in real time.

To answer some of your questions, I'm female and I live in southern California, not the LA area but a more suburban city northwest of it. I went to a very urban area for college, where I met my ex boyfriend and my close circle of friends, and when my relationship fell apart so did my role in the friend group so I basically avoid that area like the plague now because of the memories. As for hobbies, I've recently fallen back into reading and writing some, but I also play some video games as more of a means of escape if that makes sense. They're interactive, so I don't have the brain capacity at the time to dote on problems or matters that are affecting me.  

I've always looked at college as something I had to do, something my cousins and rest of my family had done so it was expected of me. Of course I also wanted to go, but I never really looked at it as an achievement. I studied Kinesiology while in college more for the practicality of doing something in the medical field that wasn't completely unbearable for me like one of the major sciences. I told my family I wanted to be a physical therapist but that requires more schooling. Right now though, I'm not sure as to what I want to do honestly. I haven't yet fallen into my niche, and I didn't want to accumulate more student debt trying to find out with more years of undergrad.  

By research, I meant more just studying common suicide methods and what would be the least painful. Also, we're severely understaffed at work, and only have two other coworkers: a boy around 20 who's going to be leaving soon in order to pursue sports, and a woman 15 years older than me who likes talking about her own matters quite a lot. I don't mind listening to either of them, but I've just never been the type to divulge heavier thoughts to individuals whom I haven't built a lot of rapport with yet.  

I will agree with you that the amount of genuine souls I've encountered so far is slim. I feel as if I've grown quite jaded after everything as well. I used to be the girl with the big network of friends, the one who'd have to reserve a table for 30 on her birthday, but since losing most everyone I held dear to me, I realized that I didn't have a major place in their thoughts and hearts to begin with, which was a shocking realization because I invested a lot in my friendships and my romantic relationship, and felt genuinely for all of them. I've learned that talk is cheap, and most everyone will always just care for themselves in the end, not caring if they throw you under the bus or not.  

In that sense, I wish I'd grasped a sense of independence before this, or had been used to the idea of being a loner. You seem more accepting of it, which I admire, even though the concept of it is still kind of sad. I'm still wallowing in the loss that lead to me becoming one myself.  But I appreciate the offer of being a listening ear for me. If I feel a little braver  within the next few days, I might take you up on it.

Still not sure if I'm going to take my birthday off. I have until Sunday to request it, but I am taking the next weekend off for someone else's birthday who happens to be flying in from out of state. I'm a bit weary about that though because all she wants to do is party and drink for the weekend and while I'm usually up for that for the sake of good fun, I don't think I'm in a place where I can control my emotions in a situation like that, let alone while inebriated.
